item.title: Kentucky golf course shut after low turnout is becoming a 225-acre park, 70% greenspace
item.description: A Kentucky county closed its 225-acre Fox Run Golf Course after it averaged just 9,000 to 10,000 rounds annually. Now, the former golf property is being transformed into a major public park featuring trails, climbing areas, biking facilities, water features and family spaces. Around 70% of the site will remain preserved as natural greenspace for future generations.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Wiltshire couple face demolition of home they built for disabled daughter in 2022 after planning row
item.description: A Wiltshire couple who built a four-bedroom home for their disabled daughter in 2022 now face a council demolition order following a planning dispute. The property, built on Green Belt land, includes a basement and decking that were not part of the approved plans. The couple have appealed to the Planning Inspectorate, with a decision expected in autumn.

item.title: US halts visa appointments globally amid Trump's immigration crackdown
item.description: United States visa appointments are paused worldwide for consular officer training. This initiative supports the administration's broader immigration enforcement efforts. Immigrant visa applicants are being notified of rescheduled interviews due to this program. The government is also tightening restrictions on legal immigration and visa issuances. These actions reflect ongoing reviews and adjustments to the US visa system.
item.dc:creator: Yashasvi Vasistha

item.title: Singapore sends 70 tonnes of unwanted clothes to Malaysia to recycle
item.description: Singapore sends up to seventy tonnes of clothing weekly to Malaysia for recycling. This cross-border initiative gives discarded garments a second life through reuse and repurposing. The volume has doubled in two years, highlighting the growing scale of textile waste management. At the Malaysian facility, clothes are sorted for resale or material recovery. This partnership aims to keep textiles in circulation and reduce landfill disposal.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Port Houston donates $500,000 to 32 nonprofits for community programmes
item.description: In a significant move to bolster local communities, Port Houston has allocated $500,000 among 32 organizations focused on enhancing workforce training, educational resources, and health initiatives. A noteworthy portion of this funding is devoted to developing maritime career opportunities. Starting in 2027, upcoming grants will be aligned with the strategic Anchored in Action plan, reinforcing community development along the Houston Ship Channel region.

item.title: In 2022, CaseOh was mowing lawns for work; two years later, he won Content Creator of the Year
item.description: CaseOh’s creator journey moved at a ridiculous speed. In 2022, Case Dylan Baker was doing maintenance work with his father in rural Arkansas while making NBA 2K TikToks after work. His clips soon brought thousands of followers and pushed him onto Twitch. By December 2024, he had beaten several major creators to win Content Creator of the Year at The Game Awards.
item.dc:creator: Global Sports Desk

item.title: Jimmy Donaldson started YouTube at 13; years later the channel turned into a $5 billion business
item.description: Jimmy Donaldson started uploading YouTube videos as a 13-year-old in Eastern North Carolina. Years of low-view uploads, intense YouTube analysis and aggressive reinvestment helped turn MrBeast into a massive media and business operation. From viral challenges and Feastables to Beast Mobile, Step and Beast Games, Donaldson’s channel became the foundation of Beast Industries, now valued at roughly $5.2 billion.
item.dc:creator: Global Sports Desk

item.title: Speed Urges Camden On: IShowSpeed shares hard-won advice; viral rise tests Nitro Camden
item.description: IShowSpeed met Nitro Camden after the young streamer’s family situation went viral and encouraged him to keep chasing his goals. Speed said he had faced similar pressure from his own mother early in his streaming career. Camden became emotional during the meeting. His future plans remain unclear, but the conversation gave him support from one of streaming’s biggest names today.
item.dc:creator: Sumit Roy

item.title: Watch: US military's 'lethal kinetic strike' destroys drug boat in Caribbean; 4 killed
item.description: The US military conducted a strike on a boat in the Caribbean Sea. This operation resulted in the deaths of four individuals suspected of drug trafficking. Another strike in the eastern Pacific Ocean killed two people accused of similar activities. These recent attacks bring the total killed in such operations to at least 227. Human rights groups have criticized these actions as unlawful extrajudicial killings.

item.title: In 1957, Georgia artist Eddie Owens Martin began transforming his inherited farmhouse and seven acres
item.description: Eddie Owens Martin, an innovative and unconventional artist, dedicated nearly three decades to transforming his land in Georgia into the vibrant, visionary art space known as Pasaquan. He intricately combined various cultural elements through his painted totems and impressive masonry. After years of exposure and deterioration, the Kohler Foundation intervened with a major restoration, breathing new life into this unique site.

item.title: In 1903, rabbits were released on Hawaii’s Laysan Island as a food source; within a decade...
item.description: German immigrant Max Schlemmer introduced rabbits to Laysan Island in 1903 for business and entertainment. These rabbits rapidly consumed vegetation, leading to the extinction of three unique landbird species. President Theodore Roosevelt established the Hawaiian Islands Bird Reservation to protect the remaining wildlife. Federal authorities later removed Schlemmer and eradicated the invasive rabbit population by 1923. Conservationists have since worked to restore the habitat and reintroduce species to the island.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: New Mexico has protected nearly 11,000 acres along the Mimbres River as a new wildlife area
item.description: In a significant conservation achievement, officials in New Mexico have successfully acquired nearly eleven thousand acres of lush land along the Mimbres River, now designated as a public preserve. This initiative not only safeguards essential water rights and desert habitats for indigenous wildlife but also enhances public access while fostering tourism and outdoor activities. The long-term impact of this effort will greatly benefit the environment and local communities.

item.title: Georgia sheriff’s office arrested a second deputy in one month over alleged Flock misuse
item.description: In a troubling turn of events, a second deputy from Habersham County, Jonathan Thomas, has been dismissed and arrested for misusing surveillance technology. He reportedly accessed the license plate reader system for personal use, following a similar incident involving former deputy Christian Brewer. As a response, the sheriff's office is enhancing regulations around sensitive data access, part of a broader state investigation into data misuse incidents.
